propositions: Bridge-shaped operations (preview, sync, status, pause, resume, access-check) must be exposed as typed public library functions and MCP tools with explicit options, not mode strings.

Legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck() interfaces must retain their published defaults, accepted mode values, return types, exception behavior, and mutation boundaries as compatibility entrypoints.

New bridge operations and their legacy mode-mapped equivalents must use the same canonical route/disposition classification through run_pass() and _Disposition rather than duplicate or invoke the CLI.
MCP mcp.allow_jira_sync gate must reject mutating routes (bridge_sync, bridge_pause, bridge_resume, mutating reconcile modes) while allowing read-only paths (preview, status, fsck, access-check).
Every new structured-result MCP tool must publish an outputSchema and remain in parity with the public result types, while existing compatibility tool schemas remain valid.
Documentation must present noun-based bridge operations as primary APIs while explicitly documenting retained compatibility mappings for legacy callers.
